Synopsis:
After being defeated in combat, a goblin named Fezzerk begs for mercy from the player. He tries to bargain for his life. The player can let him go or kill him. This dialogue takes place somewhere away from the windmill where Fezzerk was tormenting Barcus Wroot.

Cluster Contexts:
- FOR_GnomeGoblin1_Surrender_NotAtWindmill.json: Fezzerk is a goblin the player just defeated in a fight — he’d been tormenting Barcus Wroot at the windmill earlier but this pleading scene occurs away from that location. Panicked and desperate, he begs for mercy and frantically offers bribes or “useful” information to bargain for his life; he may be lying or exaggerating to survive. The player has an immediate, binary choice in this single, self‑contained encounter: spare him (he will likely try to flee or renege) or kill him outright. There is no deeper prior relationship implied here — this is a short, consequential follow‑up to the combat.
- DEN_CapturedGoblin_Caged.json: Character is caged for this entire dialogue If the player saves the goblin captive from being killed, the goblin will try to convince the player to free them and then meet the player later in the goblin camp.
- DEN_CapturedGoblin.json: If the player saves the goblin captive from being killed, the goblin will try to convince the player to free them and then meet the player later in the goblin camp. Note from Swen on this dialogue: ''I also want a different emotion in there. This goblin is negotiating with me. Think a terrorist that is locked up and who is offering their interrogators an option to save their lives if they free her.
It'll be quite the intense conversation.''
- GOB_AftermathTrader.json: After Goblin Hunt Celebration night and persuading Minthara to spare their lives, player can observe Goblin camp being empty with only one goblin trader looting what's rest in the Festivities area.This is that goblin's dialog.
- FOR_GnomeGoblin1.json: The party finds three goblins tormenting a bound deep gnome (Barcus Wroot) by tying him to a windmill sail and jeering as he spins; Fezzerk is the boastful leader who taunts the captive and demands an absurd “toll” from anyone who tries to pass. If the player bears a cult symbol/True Soul mark it can glow and intimidate Fezzerk into withdrawing, though using that mark produces an unsettling, hunger‑like reaction in the player. Goblins react to PC race — a drow player will make them far more nervous and easier to cow. The captive occasionally cries out (pleading, panicked, or insulting), and off‑screen there may be wider goblin activity and refugee/druid tensions in the region that don’t need to be resolved to play this scene.

context: Fezzerk is a goblin the party previously saw tormenting Barcus Wroot at the windmill, but this exchange occurs after you defeated him in combat and away from the mill. Panicked and desperate, he grovels and frantically offers bribes or “useful” information to bargain for his life—claims he may be lying or exaggerating to survive. The player faces an immediate, binary choice in this short, self‑contained scene: spare him (he will likely try to flee or renege, and in some variants may later press you to free him or arrange a meeting at the goblin camp) or kill him outright. No deeper prior relationship is implied beyond this consequential follow‑up to the fight.
